text.p: Texaco Inc said on Wednesday that it has agreed to study and pursue the development of extra-heavy crude oil in the Hamaca region in Venezuela.
Texaco will enter the venture with Corpoven, a unit of Petroleos de Venezuela SA, Atlantic Richfield Co and Phillips Petroleum Co, the company said.

A top Venezuelan oil official said on Monday that Texaco and Phillips will enter the $3.5 billion venture in Venezuela's Orinoco Belt, which is believed to contina approximately 1.2 trillion barrels of extra-heavy crude.
Texaco, which will hold a 20 percent stake in the project said Corpoven and Atlantic Richfield will each hold 30 percent, while Phillips will own 20 percent.
Of the 1.2 trillion barrels of extra heavy crude, 270 billion barrels are currently considered recoverable in the Orinoco belt.
At the Hamaca site, 2.4 billion barrels are expected to be recovered with production peaking at nearly 200,000 barrels per day over a 35-year production period, Texaco said.
Initial production is scheduled in early 1999, Texaco said.

Texaco said the crude would be transported by pipeline to an upgrading plant to be constructed on the Caribbean coast of Venezuela where it would be processed using state-of-the-art upgrading technology into a marketable 25-degree API gravity oil resembling Alaska North Slope crude.
After processing, the crude would be exported and sold on the open market, the company said.
Phillips said in a separate statement that the Hamaca project could involve drilling more than 700 new wells, most of them horizontal.

The Hamaca venture is expected to produce an average of 36,000 barrels of oil per day from mid-1999 to 2001, 100,000 barrels per day from 2002 to 2005 and 197,000 barrels per day from 2006 to 2036, Phillips said.
